title: Free-Throw Routine Builder
description: Young players design their own short, repeatable free-throw routine (dribbles, breath, look) and practise it until it is automatic.

content.objective: Create and repeat a personal free-throw routine that takes about five seconds and stays the same every time.
content.setup: Players at the free-throw lines of available baskets (shorter distance for younger players).
content.organization: Players take turns; teammates check the routine is identical.
instructions: Choose a routine: e.g. three dribbles, a deep breath, eyes on the front of the rim.
Say the routine out loud once, then do it silently.
Shoot five free throws with the routine.
A teammate checks that each one was the same.
coachingPoints: Short and simple: under ten seconds.
Same every time, make or miss.
Breath out before the shot to relax.
commonMistakes: A routine that changes after misses.
content.safety: Shooters rebound their own ball only when the lane is clear; nobody stands under the rim while others shoot.
progressions: Use the routine after a sprint.
regressions: Shoot from a step inside the line.
variations: Routine for the first and second shot.
successCriteria: Routine identical on five shots in a row.
content.gameApplication: A routine calms nerves and makes the free throw feel the same in any game.
